Sam — thanks for the context and the report. Quick high level proposal below; I'll put this into a short one-pager and a draft amendment for legal to review.

Summary proposal (in-principle)
- Term: 3 years, start 2027-10-01, co-term to calendar year (Jan 1) on finalization.
- Staged ramp (stair-step): Year1 = 60% of projected peak commit, Year2 = 85%, Year3 = 110% (auto-adjust at each anniversary based on agreed usage banding).
- Conversion credits: unused committed units roll into a credit bank usable for burst months (up to 20% of monthly overage). Credits expire on next anniversary unless converted into prepay for Dedicated capacity.
- Dedicated migration: allow pinned Dedicated pools to be brought online mid-term; co-terming keeps billing aligned and racks capacity to your account.
- Auto-renew: opt-in by default with 60-day opt-out notice; we can add a procurement exemption carve-out.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly — can you confirm whether finance is ok with the 20% credit cap and the expiry mechanics?
2) Marissa — can you draft amendment + SOW migration plan to share with BigCloud legal and procurement?
3) Sam/Laura — can we schedule a 30m call 7/7 or 7/12 to walk the proposal before the 7/20 procurement meeting?

I'll attach a short playbook and sample amendment in next email.

— Jonas

(signature)

Agree with the construct; two internal asks from finance/proc:

- Escrow-like smoothing window: propose a 90-day carry-forward window for credits instead of single-anniversary expiry — this helps procurement forecast monthly burn and reduces churn.
- True-up trigger: for Year2/3 automatic uplift, require a 30-day notice and allow a one-time reversal if usage falls >15% vs forecast (protects both sides).

Also, recommend we include a small onboarding credit (one month at 30%) if they move >40% of workloads to Dedicated within first 6 months — lowers their migration friction.

I can run numbers with finance once Sam confirms approximate expected monthly peak (you have the CSV).

Kimberly
Director, Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference
